public_payload.normalized_proposition: Unless Anthropic is making over $100 billion within two years, it cannot afford its commitments.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic needs to be making over $100 billion in two years or it can’t afford its commitments

from_speaker: or it can’t afford its commitments
our_interpretation: This asserts a necessary revenue level for affordability, rather than simply predicting that revenue will exceed $100 billion.
I read 'in two years' as June 8, 2028, and 'making' as annual realized revenue, consistent with the surrounding discussion of annual revenue.
For an anniversary-date assessment, annual revenue means the trailing twelve months ending June 8, 2028. Fiscal-year figures would require reconciliation.
Affordability means the ability to meet contractual payments when due, considering operating cash flow, existing cash, and available financing.
The revenue level and affordability are the joint outcomes being tested. 'To afford its commitments' supplies no separate external antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence for the deadline establishes that annual revenue of $100 billion or less cannot fund the relevant payments even after available cash and financing are considered, and demonstrates why revenue exceeding that threshold is necessary.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Anthropic has annual revenue of $100 billion or less at the deadline while demonstrably retaining sufficient resources to meet the relevant commitments when due.
